title: Mit csináltál vele? What Did You Do With It?

sections.title: csinál in the past, plus -val/-vel
sections.content: Once you've bought, found, or met something or someone, the natural next question is Mit csináltál vele? ("What did you do with it/him/her?") — csinál ("to do, make") is fully regular, and vele is the same -val/-vel pronoun you already use for people. Once you've already named the thing, swap it for vele instead of repeating the noun, exactly the way you already do with people: Megvettem a kabátot, aztán felvettem. is just as natural as ...aztán felvettem a kabátot.

sections.title: csinál + vele
rows: What did you do with it?
What did you do with the coat?
I didn't do anything with it.
What did Károly do with the gift?

items.spanish: Megvettem a kabátot, aztán rögtön felvettem.
items.english: I bought the coat, then put it on right away.
I paid with it (the card) at the store.
What did you do with the old coat?

sections.content: vele works for a thing just as easily as for a person — vele covers "with it" and "with him/her" both, so once you've named the object once, you rarely repeat it.
